LG Extended Electricity still restricts controller reach. Turn off "Mod sets generator range" and "Mod sets generator vertical range" in sandbox settings, then restart the server or reload your singleplayer save. Changing the options alone does not restore the range.

Lets players convert generators into Off-Grid backups. Off stops the ones that are running and refuses new conversions; Convert to normal generator still works.
How much gasoline a backup generator burns. 1 burns what a normal generator burns for the same appliances, or in Realistic Mode what a real generator burns. 0 is free.
Scales how much every battery stores.
Storage barns with spare solar gear (one in)
On newly explored ground, one hay-storage barn in this many holds a few spare panels and battery racks. 0 means none.
Running batteries flat costs capacity permanently. Cheap chemistries start suffering far sooner than sealed ones.
How far a transformer's power line can run, to the controller or to another transformer, in tiles.
How far each component reaches to find the next one. Banks chain, so a run of them can lead away from the controller.
Scales everything the panels make. 100 is the physical model.
Who may pick up solar parts
Whoever placed it, their safehouse, admins and moderators

Panels and battery banks are expensive to build and trivial to carry off. Mods that remove the tool requirement for moving furniture otherwise make every rig free to take. On a server this also decides who may use a rig's controls: switching a controller, its cables, wiring buildings, and a backup generator's switches and fuel barrels. Anyone nearby may still read the monitor, clean panels, and refuel or repair a backup.

Panels make what panels made in 1993: three modules of about 50 W to a frame, so a standard frame gives about 140 W in full sun, a quarter of the usual. Makeshift frames make about half that, premium frames a little more. Backup generators burn gasoline like real generators: 0.15 L an hour for each kW of their rating, plus 0.45 L for each kWh they deliver.
Houses with a solar rig (one in)
On newly explored ground, one house in this many has a solar rig in the yard. 0 means none.
Count what the lights, fridges and ovens in range are drawing. Off means the system only ever charges.
How fast snow covers the glass. 0 means it never settles. Roof panels collect faster and shed slower whatever this is set to.
How fast dirt cuts output. Rain washes panels either way.
What each transformer draws while the system has power, even with nothing switched on.
A proper tilted array. Point it south, keep it clear of roofs, sweep the snow off in winter.
Monocrystalline cells on an aluminium frame. Twice the array of the standard frame, and it barely notices the heat.
Cannibalised cells on a scrap frame. Weak, and the weather eats it, but it is a panel and it is free.
A Lectromax generator converted for Off-Grid. It gives 4,000 W and only ever feeds the controller it is cabled to.
An old generator converted for Off-Grid. It gives 3,000 W and only ever feeds the controller it is cabled to.
A Premium Technologies generator converted for Off-Grid. It gives 5,000 W and only ever feeds the controller it is cabled to.
A ValuTech generator converted for Off-Grid. It gives 2,500 W and only ever feeds the controller it is cabled to.
An open steel rack for six car batteries. Running it flat costs capacity for good.
Three car batteries strapped to a pallet. Small, leaky, and it hates being run flat.
Eight sealed deep-cycle cells in a vented cabinet. Holds its charge in the cold and forgives a deep discharge.
Ties the arrays and the banks together and powers everything nearby. Silent, unlike a generator.
Tracks each array's maximum power point. Ten per cent more out of the same panels, and a better readout.
Lies almost flat, so it wins the summer and loses the winter. Snow sits on it until you climb up and sweep it.
The best cells on the lowest frame. Enormous in July, disappointing in January.
Salvaged cells on a low frame for a rooftop. Cheap, and out of reach of anything on the ground.
A knee-high light with its own little panel and battery. It charges in the sun and lights the path from dusk to dawn. Needs no wiring.
A street light on a pole, with its own panel and battery pack. It charges all day and lights the road from dusk to dawn. Needs no wiring.

Carries the controller's power across town. Run a cable to the controller or to another transformer. While the system has power it lights everything around it, as far as the controller reaches, and it can wire up a building.
A three-cell box that bolts to a wall. Half the storage of the rack, none of the footprint.
Two batteries on a plank shelf. Takes no floor space and not much else either.
Four sealed cells in a wall cabinet. The tidy way to fill a battery room.
It holds something besides gasoline. Empty it first.
This barrel already feeds a generator.

Makes it a backup for an Off-Grid controller: run a cable from it to one and the controller starts and stops it. If Off-Grid is removed from this save, this generator is removed with it. Convert it to a normal generator first.

Starts a generator when the batteries run low, and stops it when they are nearly full or the sun has taken over.
This generator model can't be converted.

Not connected to a controller. Run a cable from it to one.

Coverage on your current floor. Green: supplying power. Amber: no power. Lights and appliances in reach glow green when switched on, white when switched off. Press Esc to hide.
You need a rag and some water.
Painted with the Brush Tool: not a working controller.
Too heavy for what you are carrying.
Stops powering the buildings this part wired. Its own reach stays.
Powers every floor of the building this stands in or next to, whenever the system has power. Power can reach a few tiles past its walls. Whatever runs in there draws on the batteries.
Knowledge of reading the coming weather from the sky.
